differences.detail: Prior is labeled PA. Current is labeled AP portable.
differences.prevents: Comparison of heart size, mediastinal width and the size of any lesion. AP projection magnifies anterior structures.

differences.detail: Current is labeled supine. Prior position is not marked on the image and has the appearance of an upright film.
differences.prevents: Judging presence or change of pleural effusion, which layers posteriorly when supine, and excluding pneumothorax or free subdiaphragmatic gas. Supine position also widens the mediastinum and makes upper zone vessels more prominent.

differences.detail: Prior has adequate inspiration. Current has low lung volumes with elevated hemidiaphragms.
differences.prevents: Calling new basal opacity, increased interstitial markings or cardiac enlargement, because low volumes crowd the lower zones and enlarge the heart shadow.

differences.detail: Both films appear mildly rotated, and the degree is hard to match between them.
differences.prevents: Reliable comparison of hilar size, tracheal position and left-right lung density.

systematic_read.airway_lungs: CURRENT: Trachea is approximately midline, allowing for rotation and overlying linear densities. Lung volumes are low. There are bilateral hazy and coarse reticular opacities in the perihilar, mid and lower zones, with denser hazy opacity at the right base and in the left retrocardiac and basal region. No lobar collapse is evident. PRIOR: Trachea is approximately midline. Lungs are well inflated. Bronchovascular markings are mildly prominent in the perihilar regions and right lower zone, with no confluent opacity. The left retrocardiac region is partly obscured by the heart.
systematic_read.mediastinum_hila: CURRENT: Upper mediastinum appears wide, which is expected on a supine AP film with low volumes. Hila are indistinct and partly obscured by perihilar opacity and device leads. PRIOR: Mediastinal contour is within expected limits for the projection, with a prominent aortic knuckle. Hila are not clearly enlarged. Hilar and mediastinal size cannot be compared between the two films.
systematic_read.pleura: CURRENT: No pleural line is seen to suggest pneumothorax, though a supine film is insensitive for this. Both costophrenic angles are hazy and poorly defined, so layering effusions are not excluded. PRIOR: No pneumothorax is seen. The right costophrenic angle is at the image edge and appears grossly clear. The left costophrenic angle shows no large effusion.
systematic_read.heart: CURRENT: Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged, but the film is AP supine with low volumes, so size is not reliable. PRIOR: Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged on the PA film. Change in heart size between the studies cannot be assessed.
systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Both hemidiaphragms are elevated and indistinct, consistent with low volumes and adjacent basal opacity. No free gas is identified, but a supine film is insensitive for it. PRIOR: Both hemidiaphragms are well defined, with the right dome slightly higher than the left. No free subdiaphragmatic gas is seen.
systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT and PRIOR: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion is seen at this image resolution. Degenerative change is present at the shoulders. No soft tissue gas is seen. Fine bone detail is limited on both, more so on the portable film.
systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with multiple transvenous leads, including shock-coil segments projected over the right paramediastinal region and the lower cardiac silhouette. External ECG electrodes and wires are present. Additional linear tubular densities project over the tracheal air column and upper mediastinum and cannot be characterized with certainty. PRIOR: The same type of left chest wall generator with multiple leads, with coil segments over the right mediastinal border and lower left cardiac silhouette. No other tubes or lines are seen.

findings.description: Hazy and coarse reticular opacity in the right perihilar and mid zone, more conspicuous on the current film than on the prior.
findings.evidence: Prior PA film with good inspiration shows only mildly prominent markings. Current AP supine low-volume film shows denser perihilar and mid zone markings. Low volumes, supine position and the exposure difference could account for part or all of the change.

findings.description: Hazy and coarse reticular opacity in the left perihilar and mid zone, more conspicuous on the current film than on the prior.
findings.evidence: Left mid zone markings are denser on the current film, in a distribution similar to the right side. Bilateral perihilar distribution, if real, would be consistent with interstitial fluid, but technique differences could explain the appearance.

findings.description: Hazy increased density at the right base with an indistinct right hemidiaphragm on the current film. The right base was clear on the prior.
findings.evidence: Right hemidiaphragm is sharply defined on the prior and ill defined on the current. The current film is supine with low volumes, which crowds the base and lets pleural fluid layer, so basal airspace opacity, atelectasis and layering effusion cannot be separated.

findings.description: Increased density in the left retrocardiac and basal region with an indistinct left hemidiaphragm on the current film.
findings.evidence: Left hemidiaphragm is traceable on the prior and obscured on the current. The enlarged cardiac silhouette, low volumes and supine AP technique all contribute to retrocardiac density.

findings.description: Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged on both studies.
findings.evidence: The heart appears enlarged on the PA prior. On the current AP supine low-volume film the silhouette is magnified, so no interval change in size can be stated.

findings.description: Left chest wall cardiac device generator with multiple transvenous leads, including shock-coil segments, present on both studies.
findings.evidence: Generator and lead configuration are of the same type on both films. No gross lead discontinuity is seen. Apparent differences in lead tip position are within what the projection and inspiration change can produce and cannot be judged further.

findings.description: Linear tubular densities projected over the tracheal air column and upper mediastinum on the current film, not seen on the prior. These may be support tubes or lines, or external tubing and wires.
findings.evidence: The prior shows no tube or line in this region. On the current film the densities overlap device leads, ECG wires and the spine, so their nature and tip position cannot be confirmed at this resolution.

cant_determine.recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT if clinically needed.

cant_determine.recommend: Repeat upright film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest. Correlate with clinical status.

cant_determine.question: Is there a pneumothorax or free subdiaphragmatic gas on the current study?

cant_determine.recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest.

cant_determine.recommend: Matched PA and lateral films and device interrogation if there is clinical concern.

response.limits: This is a blind first read with no indication or study dates, comparing a PA prior with an AP supine portable current film taken at low lung volumes. Size comparisons, heart size change and effusion assessment are not reliable across these techniques. Both images are downsampled, so fine detail such as small nodules, subtle rib lesions and line or tube tips needs review on the source images in PACS. The cardiac device and ECG hardware obscure parts of the left upper and mid zones and the mediastinum. No lateral view is available. All findings are draft observations for resident and attending review.
